H1: We predict religious affiliation (Religion_type) (categorical IV) will predict time spent living in country of birth (Country_live_time) (continuous DV).

H2: We predict casual sexual experiences and preferences (composite continuous IV; mean of soi_behave, soi_attitude, and soi_desire) will predict relationship duration (Relationship_length) (continuous DV).

## 1. Load the package and data
```{r load, message=FALSE}
library(codebook)

#load data/raw/data_doctored.csv
raw <- read.csv("data/raw/data_doctored.csv")

dim(raw)
str(raw)

#get variables for H1 & H2
data <- raw[, c("ResponseId", "Religion_type", "Country_live_time", "Relationship_status", "Relationship_length", 
                "soi_behave", "soi_attitude", "soi_desire")]

dim(raw)
str(raw)
```

## 2. Check participant IDs
```{r participant_ids}

## 2. Check participant IDs
#may be redundant but also trying to follow how John did this during section
summary(data$ResponseId)

#count na 
#counts na in response ID (by taking the sum)
sum(is.na(data$ResponseId))

#count blank
#this is excluding na values (the true part of the function)
sum(data$ResponseId == "", na.rm = TRUE)

#count duplicates
sum(duplicated(data$ResponseId))

#inspect records with missing or blank IDs
missingID <- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
data[missingID, ]
print(data[missingID, ])

#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]

#verify removal of row after running this code by putting dim(data) in terminal
```

## 3. Recode Religious Affiliation
```{r Religion_type}
# codebook: 1 = Christianity, 2 = Islam, 3 = Hinduism, 4 = Buddhism, 5 = Other, 6 = Judaism, 7 = None
table(data$Religion_type, useNA = "ifany")

#turn Religion_type into a factor with labels
data$Religion_type <- factor(data$Religion_type, levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7),
                             labels = c("Christianity", "Islam", "Hinduism", "Buddhism", "Other", "Judaism", "None"))
#rerun this to see the update of the names (which succesfully turned into a factor)
table(data$Religion_type, useNA = "ifany")
```


## 4. Validate Time Living in Country of Birth
```{r Country_live_time}
#from the codebook --> Country_live_time is measured in years. Valid responses are 1-80
summary(data$Country_live_time)

#count NAs
sum(is.na(data$Country_live_time))

#count responses outside 1-80
sum(!data$Country_live_time %in% 1:80 & !is.na(data$Country_live_time))

#define LiveTimeValid: Time present & within 1-80
data$LiveTimeValid <- !is.na(data$Country_live_time) & data$Country_live_time %in% 1:80

#check with table below
table(data$LiveTimeValid)

#make h1Data with ID, Religion_Type, and Country_live_time
h1Data <- data[data$LiveTimeValid & !is.na(data$Religion_type), 
               c("ResponseId", "Religion_type", "Country_live_time")]
```

## 5. SOI & Relationship Duration
```{r SOI & Relationship Duration}
#make relData for respondents currently in a relationship
#include Dating (1), In a committed relationship (2), & married (3)
table(data$Relationship_status, useNA = "ifany")
relData <- data[data$Relationship_status %in% c(1, 2, 3), ]

#define the items to check; all three use response codes 1-9
#soi_behave, soi_attitude, and soi_desire: higher codes indicate more unrestricted sociosexuality 
soi_vars <- c("soi_behave", "soi_attitude", "soi_desire")

#check the summaries and missing responses
summary(relData[, soi_vars])
colSums(is.na(relData[, soi_vars]))

#inspect the response frequencies for each item
for(i in soi_vars) {
  print(i)
  print(table(relData[, i], useNA = "ifany"))
}

#replace anything outside 1 through 9 with NA
for (i in soi_vars) {
  relData[, i] <- ifelse(relData[, i] %in% 1:9, relData[, i], NA)
}
```

## 6. Calculate SOI composite 
```{r SOI Composite}
#group variables
comVars <- c("soi_behave", "soi_attitude", "soi_desire")

#calculate the composite as the mean of all 3 variables
relData$soiComposite <- rowMeans(relData [, comVars], na.rm = TRUE)

#check score
summary(relData$soiComposite)

#check relationship length (codebook values are 1-80)
summary(relData$Relationship_length)
sum(is.na(relData$Relationship_length))

#count values out of 1-80
summary(!relData$Relationship_length %in% 1:80 & !is.na(relData$Relationship_length))

#make h2Data with ID, SOI composite, and relationship length
#keep participants with SOI composite and valid relationship length
#do not apply the H1 residence-time filter to this hypothesis 
h2Data <- relData [!is.na(relData$soiComposite) & relData$Relationship_length %in% 1:80,
                   c("ResponseId", "soiComposite", "Relationship_length")]
```

## 7. Check the final tables
```{r final_tables}
#check rows, columns, types, and missing values in h1Data
table(h1Data$Religion_type, useNA = "ifany")
range(h1Data$Country_live_time)
range(h2Data$soiComposite)
range(h2Data$Relationship_length)
#The expected ranges are 1-80 for country residence time and relationship duration, and 1-9 for the SOI mean.

```

## 8. Add labels and generate codebooks
```{r variable_labels}
#add a description to each h1Data column, in column order
#include the source codes, meaning, and units
var_label(h1Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Religious affiliation: original codes 1 = Christianity, 2 = Islam, 3 = Hinduism, 4 = Buddhism, 5 = other, 6 = Judaism, 7 = None; 
  now stored as a factor",
  "Time spent living in country of birth (Country_live_time); 1-80 years "
)

#add a description to each h2Data column, in column order
#include response anchors and the commitment scoring rule
var_label(h2Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Casual sexual experiences and preferences: mean of available soi_behave, soi_attitude, and soi_desire responses (each 1-9); 
  no reverse coding; at least one valid response required",
  "Length of current relationship (Relationship_length): years; 1 = one year or less, 2 = 79 corresponding years, 80-80 years or more"
)

#generate the h1Data codebook
compact_codebook(h1Data)


#generate the h2Data codebook
compact_codebook(h2Data)
```

## 9. Save the final tables
```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(h1Data,"data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(h2Data,"data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
h1Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv")
dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)
```
